questions.q: What is Salesforce's standard batch size for a record-triggered flow?
options: Up to 200 records in a single transaction
Always exactly 1 record
Up to 2,000 records in a single transaction
There is no limit on batch size
questions.explain: Record-triggered flows can process up to 200 records together in a single transaction — a data import, API batch, or mass action commonly triggers that many at once.

questions.q: What specifically causes performance problems in an unbulkified flow?
options: Using too many Decision elements
A Get Records, Create Records, Update Records, or Delete Records element placed inside a Loop, re-running once per record
Using Screen elements in an autolaunched flow
Naming variables with underscores
questions.explain: A DML or query element inside a loop issues one database operation per record instead of one per batch, multiplying queries and writes by the batch size.

questions.q: In the bulkified pattern from this lesson, how many Update Records calls run for a 200-record batch?
options: 200, one per record
0 — updates are skipped entirely
1, against the whole collection at once
2, split into two sub-batches
questions.explain: The bulkified version collects values in memory during the loop and performs exactly one Update Records call against the entire collection.

questions.q: Why can a bulkification problem go unnoticed during normal development and testing?
options: Flow Builder automatically bulkifies every flow before saving
Testing against a handful of records in a sandbox doesn't generate enough records to hit the limits that a real mass action would
Governor limits only apply to Apex, never to Flow
Debug mode disables all governor limits
questions.explain: A flow tested against a few records looks fine; the problem surfaces the first time a real data load, integration, or mass action sends a full 200-record batch.

questions.q: What is the core fix for a loop-heavy, unbulkified flow?
options: Delete the loop and process records one at a time manually
Increase the org's governor limits in Setup
Restructure the flow so DML/query elements run once outside the loop, against a whole collection
Convert the flow into a Decision element
questions.explain: Bulkification means moving database reads and writes outside the loop so they execute once per transaction, against the full collection, not once per record.
